thread:
Maya: Quick sync - drafting the GA acceptance checklist for the new 'slices' work. Need concise gates we can present to execs.
Tom: I'll take SLA + pricing guardrails. Proposed: Hosted SLA 99.9% availability, p95 latency <150ms; Dedicated = contract SLA with reserved capacity and higher SLO.
Elena: I'll own docs. Plan: public one-pager + internal runbook with playbooks, sample prompts, and eval sets. Public doc should be minimal.
Chris: Oncall/playbooks: 24/7 paging for P0/P1 on Hosted, weekday paging for P2. Map separate rotations for Dedicated. Escalate to infra within 15m for capacity alarms.
Alex: Dedicated customers require a canary window and a capacity reservation clause. Also include a billing credit clause for missed contractual SLAs.
sre-bot: Add metrics: slice.latency.p95, slice.queue.depth, slice.model_fallbacks, slice.error.rate. Suggest synthetic smoke every hour.
Maya: Draft acceptance gates: 1) SLA sim/load tests pass, 2) public docs + internal runbook published, 3) oncall rota + documented escalation, 4) pricing/quota policy (soft + hard limits), 5) 24h synthetic smoke in staging green.
Tom: Pricing note: soft limit alert at 80%, auto-throttle at 95% for shared pools; Dedicated can override. I'll draft quota policy.
Elena: I'll publish the public stub today and drop the internal runbook template in #docs-ops.
Chris: I'll add per-slice dashboards and wire synthetic checks in staging by Friday AM.
Alex: I'll draft the Dedicated appendix and sample contract language by Friday EOD.
Maya: Ownership matrix: Product=Maya, Docs=Elena, SLA/Pricing=Tom, Oncall=Chris, Dedicated=Alex. Everyone ack?
Tom: Ack.
Elena: Ack.
Chris: Ack.
Alex: Ack.
Maya: Great. I'll assemble the one-pager for execs and circulate before EOD Friday. Ping me for blockers. :thumbsup:
